help.title: Help
help.frameColorsText: Every value carries the colour of the frame it comes from; the frame name is always shown as text. The colours are defined in config/frame-colors.json.
help.notRelevant: Grey: not relevant for the timetable
help.notRelevantText: These elements are shown in grey including their content; the frame name stays visible. Content with the same name elsewhere keeps its colour. The list is in config/not-relevant-elements.json.
help.checksText: Checks against a draft guide are labelled “checked against draft <commit>”, never “valid”.
help.guideText: The explorer reads the guide clone netexRealisationGuideSwitzerland (branch next). The guide status in the header shows the version and reports when it differs from the last tested one or the XSD is missing.
checkStatus.not_implemented: not implemented yet (planned for the first release)
check.xml_syntax.title: XML syntax
check.xml_syntax.description: Checks whether the file is well-formed XML; errors are shown with line and column.
check.references.title: References
check.references.description: Checks whether every reference (…Ref) points to an object of the expected type: resolved, unresolved, ambiguous or in a file that is not loaded. If a reference names a different version than its only target, it stays resolved and gets a note.
check.xsd.title: XSD validation
check.xsd.description: Checks every file detected as CH 2.0 with lxml against the NeTEx XSD of the guide version (xsd/xsd/NeTEx_publication.xsd). The XSD is loaded once at startup in the background (about 17 seconds). Findings are shown in the original wording of the XSD message with file and line.
check.general_rules.title: General guide rules
check.general_rules.description: The four general Schematron rules of the guide (src/schematron_rules/general_rules.sch, with lxml.isoschematron): version and versionRef never “any”, Ref elements with version or versionRef, no order attribute.
check.ch_core_rules.title: Swiss core rules for the timetable
check.ch_core_rules.description: 30 rules from the guide templates for ServiceJourney, ServiceJourneyPattern, TimeDemandType, TimingLink and JourneyPart: mandatory elements, forbidden elements (e.g. calls) and allowed values. Each rule names the template and lines in the checked commit (see section “Swiss core rules”).
check.ch_profile_rules.title: Other Swiss profile rules
check.ch_profile_rules.description: The remaining roughly 330 rules from the guide templates, later via the build tool of the guide.
feature.guide_status.title: Guide status
feature.guide_status.description: The header shows a dot with a short text (Guide: ok, deviation or error). A click expands the details: guide version in use (branch, commit), whether the XSD is present, whether this version has been tested, whether the mapping table is readable and problems with the settings files, each with a hint on what to do.
feature.frame_legend.title: Colour legend
feature.frame_legend.description: Shows, where frame colours are visible, which colour belongs to which frame: in the right column next to the XML, in the journey view with “Show origin” and in the structure overview. Grey means “not relevant for the timetable”.
feature.language_switch.title: Language switch
feature.language_switch.description: User interface in German or English. Values, codes and texts from the files are never translated.
feature.help_page.title: Help page
feature.help_page.description: This page: features, colours, checks performed and not performed, and severities, generated from the current settings.

xml.doctype_forbidden: The file contains a DOCTYPE declaration. For security reasons such files are not read.
xml.encoding_unsupported: Character encoding {encoding} is not supported (expected: UTF-8).
feature.example_selection.title: Example selection
feature.example_selection.description: All examples of the guide version, each loadable on its own: as a list in the header, on the start page as a list with description (example 01 is highlighted as the starting point). Status: ✔ no messages, ℹ/⚠ with notes or errors, ✖ not readable or “check failed” (an error in the check, not in the example), “changed since last test” or “new”.
feature.journey_list.title: Journey list
feature.journey_list.description: Tab “Journeys” on the left: one journey per row with product category and train number, below it departure, first and last stop. A click opens the journey as a timetable. Anything that cannot be resolved is marked as such. The tabs “Journeys”, “Objects” and “Check” can be reached with the Tab key and switched with the arrow keys (and Home/End).
feature.object_search.title: Object search
feature.object_search.description: Tab “Objects” on the left: simple search by object type and partial text in ID or name, page by page; the results are a single-column list.
feature.object_detail.title: Object details
feature.object_detail.description: Type, ID, frame with colour, file with line and column, path and content of an object; values unchanged from the file.
feature.xml_view.title: XML view
feature.xml_view.description: The right column appears as soon as something is selected (“Close” clears the selection and gives the width back to the main area). It shows the excerpt of the file with the selected value marked exactly and coloured frame bands at the margin.
feature.diagnostics_list.title: Diagnostics
feature.diagnostics_list.description: In the tab “Check” on the left: problems of the file with severity, kind and position; a click shows the position in the XML.
reference.unresolved: {element}: target {ref} (expected: {expected}) not found although the dataset contains objects of this type.
reference.external_or_unloaded: {element}: target {ref} (expected: {expected}) is not in this file (external or not loaded).
reference.version_differs: {element}: target {ref} has version {found}, the reference names version {version}. The reference counts as resolved because only one object has this ID.
lookup.external_or_unloaded: {ref}: not in this file (external or not loaded)
refs.truncated: References truncated: too many to display.
chain.title: Provenance
chain.empty: Select an item to see where it comes from.
feature.references.title: References
feature.references.description: Shows for each object what it refers to and what refers to it, with the colour of the target frame and the status: resolved, unresolved, ambiguous, or external / not loaded. A reference with a different version gets a note. References inside Extensions are included. Quay and ScheduledStopPoint with the same ID are told apart.
feature.provenance_chain.title: Provenance chain
feature.provenance_chain.description: Shows as coloured boxes where an item sits: frame, containing objects, the item itself and, for a reference, its target. Each box is clickable and marks the place in the XML.
feature.navigation_history.title: History
feature.navigation_history.description: "Back in history" and "Forward in history" revisit objects and items already viewed.
projection.time.departure_missing: Time not computable: the journey has no DepartureTime.
projection.time.departure_invalid: Time not computable: DepartureTime “{value}” is not a time of day in the format hh:mm:ss (local time without time zone).
projection.time.day_offset_invalid: Time not computable: DepartureDayOffset “{value}” is not a whole number.
projection.time.demand_missing: Time not computable: the journey names no TimeDemandType (TimeDemandTypeRef is missing).
projection.time.demand_unresolved: Time not computable: the TimeDemandType {ref} is not resolved in this file.
projection.time.timing_link_unresolved: Time not computable: the OnwardTimingLinkRef {ref} is not resolved.
projection.time.timing_link_not_found: Time not computable: no TimingLink from {from} to {to} found (no OnwardTimingLinkRef, and none matches via FromPointRef/ToPointRef).
projection.time.timing_link_ambiguous: Time not computable: several TimingLinks from {from} to {to} match; the choice is not unambiguous.
projection.time.run_time_missing: Time not computable: the TimeDemandType has no JourneyRunTime with RunTime for the TimingLink {link}.
projection.time.run_time_ambiguous: Time not computable: the TimeDemandType has several JourneyRunTime for the TimingLink {link}.
projection.time.wait_time_missing: Time not computable: the JourneyWaitTime for stop {position} has no WaitTime.
projection.time.wait_time_ambiguous: Time not computable: there are several JourneyWaitTime for stop {position}.
projection.time.duration_invalid: Time not computable: “{value}” is not a supported duration (e.g. PT10M expected; months and years are not a fixed duration).
projection.time.stop_unavailable: Time not computable: the scheduled stop point of stop {position} cannot be resolved; the TimingLink cannot be determined.
projection.timing_link_from_to: For legs without OnwardTimingLinkRef (number: {legs}) the TimingLink was determined via FromPointRef/ToPointRef (e.g. {link}).
projection.day_offset_default: DepartureDayOffset is missing; 0 applies as default value.
projection.stop_order_differs: The attribute order of the StopPointInJourneyPattern (not allowed) differs from the XML order. The XML order applies.
projection.part_time_differs: JourneyPart {part}: {field} {stated} (day {statedDay}) differs from the calculated time {computed} (day {computedDay}).
projection.dst_night_forward: Night of the time change on {date} (02:00 jumps to 03:00): the journey touches this hour. Times are local time without zone, so the duration is not unambiguous in this night. Nothing is corrected.
projection.dst_night_back: Night of the time change on {date} (03:00 goes back to 02:00): the journey touches the hour that occurs twice. Times are local time without zone, so the duration is not unambiguous in this night. Nothing is corrected.
projection.availability_element_missing: Operating days: the AvailabilityCondition has no {element}.
projection.availability_date_invalid: Operating days: {element} “{value}” is not a date.
projection.availability_range_invalid: Operating days: ToDate is before FromDate.
projection.availability_bits_invalid: Operating days: ValidDayBits may only consist of 0 and 1.
projection.availability_bits_length: Operating days: the length of ValidDayBits ({bits}) does not match the number of days in the period ({days}). The days are not listed because assigning bits to days would be a guess.
projection.notice_unassigned: {count} notice assignments (NoticeAssignment) at frame level name neither this journey nor its journey pattern; they are not shown here.
projection.notice_unassigned.one: 1 notice assignment (NoticeAssignment) at frame level names neither this journey nor its journey pattern; it is not shown here.

view.title: View
feature.journey_view.title: Journey view
feature.journey_view.description: Shows a journey (ServiceJourney) as a timetable display: a header with product category, train number, from → to, operator, operating days and the number of findings; below it the timetable with arrival | departure | stop (with stop line) | platform/quay | note. “Platform” is used for TransportMode rail, otherwise “Quay”. Boarding/alighting is written out only when restricted. All other details (line, means of transport, product category with master data, journey pattern, journey times type, operating days, offers, journey parts, notices) are collapsed under “More details”, the findings of the journey at the bottom. The main area can be switched between “Journey” and “Object”. A click on any value marks the place in the XML and shows the provenance chain on the right. What is missing or cannot be resolved is marked as such.
feature.calculated_times.title: Calculated times and calculation chain
feature.calculated_times.description: Arrival and departure at the stops are calculated from DepartureTime, RunTime and WaitTime and marked with the symbol Σ; the legend below the timetable explains it. A click shows the calculation chain: every summand with its own clickable source; default values (e.g. no JourneyWaitTime for a stop) are marked as such. If a summand is missing or not unambiguous, “not computable” appears with the reason, and likewise for all following times.
feature.midnight.title: Day change and time change
feature.midnight.description: Every time shows its offset to the operating day (“+1”, “−1”): explicit (DepartureDayOffset), as default value 0, or calculated by adding up. Times of journey parts (JourneyPart) are compared with the calculated ones; contradictions are warnings. Journeys in nights of the time change get a notice; nothing is corrected.
feature.operating_days.title: Operating days
feature.operating_days.description: Shows the validity and the number of operating days in the header and, under “More details”, a collapsible list of the days from the AvailabilityCondition (ValidDayBits). There are no statements like “Mon to Fri” or “daily”. If the length of the bits does not match the period, the days are not listed and a warning appears.
feature.offers.title: Offers and journey parts
feature.offers.description: Shows the offers (ServiceFacilitySet) of the whole journey and of single journey parts (JourneyPart) only, every code unchanged, with its meaning from the mapping table. The journey parts appear under “More details” with times, operating days and their assignment to the stops; the offers of a part appear in the timetable in the column “Note” at the stops it includes.
feature.notices.title: Notices
feature.notices.description: Shows under “More details” the notices (NoticeAssignment, Notice) of a journey: texts unchanged in all languages, plus scope (journey, journey pattern, stop, or section from stop to stop). Notice assignments without assignment to a journey are not shown; their number appears as a notice.
feature.master_data.title: Master data
feature.master_data.description: Codes always appear unchanged. A meaning comes only from the file itself or from the guide’s mapping table, with sheet, row and guide version; otherwise “no explanation in the master data” is shown. Transport mode codes have no explanation.
check.journey_projection.title: Plausibility of the journey view
check.journey_projection.description: When a journey is opened, checks whether the times can be calculated, whether the times of the journey parts match the calculated ones, whether ValidDayBits match the period of the AvailabilityCondition, and whether the attribute order contradicts the XML order. Findings appear as diagnostics of the kind “Journey view”, only in the journey view of that journey.

feature.open_files.title: Open file
feature.open_files.description: Open your own files: one XML file, several XML files or a ZIP file, only through the “Open file” dialog (no path input). The files go to the local backend and stay in the folder work/ only until the dataset is closed. File names are cleaned; ZIP files are subject to limits (single file, count, compression ratio); the total size applies to all files and all ZIP files of one opening together. Only .xml entries are processed. Renamed files (cleaned or duplicate) carry a note with the original name.
feature.version_detection.title: Version detection
feature.version_detection.description: Before any check, the version of each file is detected (detected, ambiguous, unknown) with reasons: namespace, version attribute, schemaLocation, comments, file name and structure. The root attribute never decides alone. Only files detected as CH 2.0 are checked against the guide version; others (e.g. NeTEx 1.10) stay viewable in the explorer. If the version is ambiguous or unknown, the check can be forced on request (“Check as CH 2.0 anyway”).
feature.validation.title: Check
feature.validation.description: In the tab “Check” on the left (with the number of findings in its label): The “Check” button runs the XSD check, the rules of the file general_rules.sch and the Swiss core rules for the timetable. Findings are shown separated by kind with file, line, column, a marker in the XML and a link to the guide chapter in the checked commit. The result reads “checked against draft <commit>”, never “valid”; the remaining profile rules are not integrated yet. A check step only counts as “performed” if at least one file was actually checked; otherwise it is listed with the reason among the steps not performed. If the version is ambiguous or unknown, the button “Check as CH 2.0 anyway” offers the check on explicit request; the result states “checked as CH 2.0 on request, version not recognised”. A recognised other version (e.g. 1.10) is never checked this way. The tool never changes files.
openFiles.hint: One XML file, several XML files or a ZIP file.
dataset.title: Opened files
detection.notChecked: This file is not checked against CH 2.0. It stays viewable in the explorer.
validation.notCheckable: No file is detected as CH 2.0; there is nothing to check.
validation.scope: Swiss core rules for the timetable checked; remaining profile rules not integrated yet.
validation.forced: Checked as CH 2.0 on request, version not recognised.
validation.forceHint: If the version is ambiguous or unknown, the check can still run against CH 2.0 on request; the result says so. A recognised other version (e.g. NeTEx 1.10) is never checked this way.
help.coreRules: Swiss core rules for the timetable
help.coreRulesText: Derived from the guide templates; each rule names the template and lines in the checked commit. Mandatory, forbidden and value rules are errors, “expected” is a note. Not checked: a missing ServiceJourneyPatternType and the sjyid obligation “if available” (decisions of 31 Oct 2026). Stub journeys (privateCodes only, e.g. in INTERCHANGE) are not subject to the journey rules and give a note.
coreRule.kind.value: {path} in {context} must have one of these values: {allowed}.
picker.label: Dataset
examples.startHere: Start here: a simple train journey
start.title: How to start
start.step1: Choose an example of the guide (or open your own file above).
start.step2: Click a journey on the left: it appears as a timetable.
start.step3: Click a value in the timetable: its origin and its place in the XML appear on the right.
tabs.title: Sections
details.title: Origin and XML
journey.showOriginHint: Frame colours, NeTEx names and extra lines are visible.
feature.show_origin.title: Show origin
feature.show_origin.description: Switch above the timetable. Off: a calm timetable display without colour bars. On: every value carries the colour bar of its frame, NeTEx names (e.g. TransportMode=rail) are shown, as are StopPlace and Quay below every stop and ForBoarding and ForAlighting; the legend of the frame colours appears as well. A click on a value shows its origin on the right in both states. If the StopPlace name differs from that of the scheduled stop point, this is visible here.
structure.title: How is this journey built?
structure.intro: Every box is an object of the file in the colour of its frame (the frame name is shown small inside). A click shows it in the XML on the right. Only what occurs in the data appears; what is missing or cannot be resolved is marked as such. Boxes with a grey outline are derived numbers, not objects of the file.
structure.stops.title: Stops, platforms and stop places
structure.stops.explain: The stops come from the journey pattern; platform and stop place come from the assignment (PassengerStopAssignment) to Quay and StopPlace in the SiteFrame.
structure.times.title: Times
structure.times.explain: The departure at the first stop is in the journey. Run times (RunTime) and wait times (WaitTime) are in the TimeDemandType; the other times are calculated from them.
structure.days.title: Operating days
structure.days.explain: The journey refers to an AvailabilityCondition; its ValidDayBits define on which days of the period the journey runs.
structure.master.title: Line, operator, product category
structure.master.explain: Line (via the journey pattern), operator and product category are objects of their own, referred to by the journey or the line.
help.structureText: Below the timetable, “How is this journey built?” expands. The overview shows in four rows which objects of the file the journey view connects: (1) journey → journey pattern → scheduled stop points → assignment → platform and stop place; (2) journey → TimeDemandType → run and wait times → calculated times; (3) journey → AvailabilityCondition → operating days; (4) journey → line, operator and product category. Every box carries the colour of its frame and can be clicked; what is missing in the file appears as “not found” or “not in the file”.
help.frameColorsWhere: The colour legend appears where colours are visible: in the right column next to the XML, in the journey view with “Show origin” and in the structure overview.
feature.structure_overview.title: Structure overview
feature.structure_overview.description: Expandable below the timetable: a small overview of boxes showing which objects of the file connect the journey (journey pattern, scheduled stop points, assignment to platform and stop place; TimeDemandType with run and wait times and the calculated times; AvailabilityCondition with operating days; line, operator, product category). Every box has the colour of its frame, names the frame in small type and opens its place in the XML on a click; each row has an explanatory sentence. Unresolved references are marked “not found”, missing items “not in the file”. The legend of the frame colours is never shown twice: if “Show origin” is on it appears at the top of the journey view, otherwise in the overview.
